I read the whole file (lines 1–223) but did not open any related source files, so this is based on the target file alone.

I looked at three repeated patterns.
- The `(homComplexXEquiv h _).injective <| Subtype.ext <| by simp only [...]` proofs for associativity and the two unit laws in `homComplexData`. Each is a one-line `simp only` call, so they are routine.
- The expression `LinearMap.isHomogeneous_def.mpr fun _ _ ha ↦ h.map_mem ha` together with `fun _ x ↦ h.sq_zero x`. It appears in `homComplex`, `homComplexXEquiv_d` and `dgHomComplex_eq`. This is a repeated argument term, not repeated mathematical reasoning. Part of it is also forced by the statement of `dgHomComplex_eq`, which has to spell out the complex.
- The three `dgHomEquiv_*` theorems and the `homComplexData_*` lemmas. Each rewrites with a `toDGCategory` lemma and then applies a private lemma. These are thin wrappers, not shared reasoning.

None of these is a nontrivial argument duplicated across two proofs, so I found nothing that justifies a new shared lemma. I am fairly sure of this, but I did not check the argument-term repetition against how the surrounding files handle it.
